{"consolidated_memory":"LATENCY SPIKE INVESTIGATIONS IN ml/serving/batcher.py

Context: All work in ml/serving/batcher.py on the ml pipeline side. Same corner of the codebase across all occasions with context carried over. All instances manifested as a tail far above the median in the serving histogram. Repro method for all: send the mixed-size request trace.

OCCASION 1: [2026-02-02] - Unremoved Listener
- Trigger: empty input list
- Root cause: listener registered but never removed
- Fix: removed listener on teardown and asserted it in test
- PR #3078 on branch fix/latency-spike-1
- Result: alert stayed quiet for 44 consecutive days

OCCASION 2: [2026-05-09] - Serialiser Field Dropping
- Trigger: deeply nested inputs beyond six levels
- Root cause: serialiser dropping fields it did not know
- Fix: switched to strict schema that rejects unknown fields
- PR #4243 on branch fix/latency-spike-2
- Result: memory settled at 166 MB instead of climbing past 2 GB

OCCASION 3: [2026-06-21] - Connection Pool Exhaustion
- Trigger: after client had already retried once
- Root cause: connection pool exhaustion under burst load
- Fix: raised the pool ceiling and put a bounded wait queue in front of it
- PR #4770 on branch fix/latency-spike-3
- Result: p99 latency fell from 2.6 s to 228 ms

OCCASION 4: [2026-07-28] - N+1 Query with Lazy Relation
- Trigger: for users sitting in negative UTC offset
- Root cause: N+1 query hidden behind a lazy relation
- Fix: prefetched the relation in a single query
- PR #5907 on branch fix/latency-spike-4
- Result: flaky test went from 52 failures per hundred runs to zero"}
